page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.4xlarge is a general-purpose, eighth-generation instance designed to deliver a balanced balance of compute capacity, system memory, and direct-attached local storage. The virtual machine runs on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor and is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It features 16 virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core using dedicated CPU allocation, accompanied by 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

A key component of the m8idb.4xlarge hardware profile is the inclusion of 950 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage. This direct-attached drive offers low-latency block access compared to network-attached volumes, making it suitable for temporary scratch space, cache layers, and high-frequency read and write operations. The instance is not equipped with discrete GPU accelerators, focusing strictly on standard x86 CPU compute tasks. Networking performance is established at a 17 Gbps baseline bandwidth, providing sustained data throughput across enterprise network fabrics without complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default.

Qualitatively, the m8idb.4xlarge delivers cost-efficient compute and fast I/O density by co-locating high-frequency Intel compute cores with local NVMe solid-state storage on a single virtual host. Because the 950 GB NVMe volume is ephemeral instance storage, data does not persist through instance stop cycles, requiring architects to implement external replication or persistent storage strategies. The instance is well-suited for relational databases requiring fast buffer pools, caching tiers like Redis or Memcached, transactional workloads, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed data processing applications.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idb.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. Operating under the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with dedicated allocation, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory at a consistent 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It incorporates 950 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, providing fast, low-latency block I/O directly attached to the virtual host. The instance has no hardware GPU accelerators and operates with a 17 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Combining dedicated compute cores, balanced memory density, and fast ephemeral NVMe storage, the m8idb.4xlarge is engineered for I/O-intensive workloads including relational database systems, high-speed caching engines, local analytics scratch spaces, and general-purpose backend services requiring high storage throughput.
